question: Do you have an easily discoverable way for external researchers to report security vulnerabilities in your systems?
Have you recently reviewed your SSL configuration to ensure that only secure protocols and ciphers are offered to clients?
Does the application enforce minimum password security requirements (e.g., a certain length, character classes, etc.)?
Do user sessions in your application expire automatically when the user is inactive?
Are firewalls used at network boundaries to restrict inbound and outbound traffic?

Is encryption and integrity protection in place for all internal network traffic that potentially carries sensitive information (including passwords, emails, files, source code, management traffic, etc.)?
Have you implemented monitoring and alerting for your network?
Do you have a process for installing operating system and application updates and security patches on servers?
Do you also have an emergency process for installing patches outside of the regular patching schedule when high-risk vulnerabilities are identified?
Are your systems configured to log security-relevant events, such as authentication, data access, etc.?
Do you retain security event logs for at least 30 days?
Do your Windows domain administrators have separate accounts with lower privileges that they use for day-to-day tasks?
Do you have procedures in place for regularly auditing administrative access to your servers?
Do you store backup media in an off-site facility that is protected against potential disaster?
Do you regularly test your backups?
Do you have controls in place to protect client systems from malware?
Are laptops and other portable devices protected with full-disk encryption?
Do you allow access to confidential information (e.g., email) from unencrypted mobile devices such as phones and tablets?
Does an independent third party regularly perform penetration tests on all systems used to provide services to customers?
Do you run vulnerability scans at least once a year?
Does your company have a strong, established security program, and does the scope of the program include all information processed as part of this project?
Is a named person or team accountable for your information security and privacy program?
How often are internal information security and privacy audits performed?

Has your company selected an individual or team to be responsible for reviewing service providers and subcontractors, to ensure that they sufficiently protect the security and privacy of sensitive information and systems?
Is your change management process formally documented, and does it classify changes by impact and size?
Do you have documented procedures for responding to security incidents?
Do you inform affected customers about security incidents?

Do you have processes in place to ensure that access to data is granted solely on a "need-to-know" basis, in accordance with the job descriptions and responsibilities of users? Do these processes also revoke access when the need no longer exists?
Do you have processes in place to make sure access (both physical and logical) is revoked when an employee, intern, vendor, contractor, or other associate leaves the company or a contract ends?
Do employees receive security training when they join?
